title: The corridor of three doors
goals: Reach the mark in the arch at the top.
starting_code:
next_door = wizard.find_nearest("door")
next_door.open()
wizard.move_up(4)
next_door = wizard.find_nearest("door")
next_door.open()
wizard.move_up(4)
next_door = wizard.find_nearest("door")
next_door.open()
wizard.move_up(4)
hints: We can make this much shorter with a loop! Look at the repeating lines.
The three lines that repeat can be put inside a `for` loop with `range(3)`.
Delete the extra lines and leave just one block of three lines inside the `for`!
intro: Look at this straight corridor... there are three exactly identical doors at the same distance! I wrote a program to open them, but it has nine lines. I bet you can do it in fewer lines with a loop. The mark is in the arch at the top.
outro: All three open, and with only four lines! On the other side, the stones look much older.
learned: Now you know that a loop repeats its lines, so three doors take four lines, and that `next_door` keeps the next door at each turn.
